title: New Zealand's New Short-Term Graduate Work Visa — Complete Guide (2026)
excerpt: New Zealand launches a brand new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa — 6 months of open work rights for graduates who don't qualify for the Post Study Work Visa. Full eligibility and conditions explained.

New Zealand Just Made It Easier to Stay After Graduation

On May 29, 2026, Immigration New Zealand made an official announcement that changes the post-graduation picture for thousands of international students. A brand new visa — the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa — will open for applications on November 16, 2026, giving eligible graduates six months of open work rights to find employment in New Zealand after completing their studies.

Alongside this, New Zealand is also extending eligibility for the existing Post Study Work Visa to include graduates who completed a Graduate Diploma at NZQCF Level 7 — also from November 16, 2026. Together, these two changes mean that significantly more international graduates will now have a structured, legal pathway to remain and work in New Zealand after finishing their qualification.

🌿
Why New Zealand is doing this New Zealand's "International Education Going for Growth" strategy — launched in July 2025 — aims to grow international student enrollments from 83,400 in 2024 to 105,000 by 2027, and to double the economic impact of international education to NZD $7.2 billion by 2034. These new visa changes are a direct part of that strategy — attracting and retaining skilled international graduates who contribute to New Zealand's workforce.

What Is the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa?

The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is a brand new visa category specifically designed for international graduates who have completed a qualification in New Zealand but whose course level does not currently qualify them for the longer Post Study Work Visa. It provides a six-month window of open work rights — meaning you can work for any employer in any role — giving you time to find employment and, where appropriate, transition to an Accredited Employer Work Visa for a longer stay.

This visa fills a significant gap in New Zealand's current post-study options. Previously, graduates with qualifications at NZQCF Level 5, 6, or 7 who did not qualify for the Post Study Work Visa had no formal post-graduation work pathway. The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa changes that entirely.

⚠️
This visa is granted once — and cannot be extended The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is a one-time, non-renewable visa. You cannot apply for a second one. Once it expires, your options are to have transitioned to an Accredited Employer Work Visa, or to leave New Zealand. Use the six months strategically from day one.

Full Eligibility Requirements — Short-Term Graduate Work Visa

To be eligible for the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa, you must meet all of the following requirements at the time of application:

  • Qualification level: You must hold a qualification at NZQCF Level 5, 6, or 7 that was studied full-time for at least 24 weeks in New Zealand. The qualification must not be an English language, foundation, or bridging program — these do not qualify.
  • Does not qualify for Post Study Work Visa: This visa is specifically for graduates whose qualification does not make them eligible for the longer Post Study Work Visa. If your qualification already qualifies for the PSWV, you should apply for that instead.
  • Minimum funds — NZD $5,000: You must demonstrate you have at least NZD $5,000 available to support yourself during the six-month visa period.
  • Medical requirements: A valid medical certificate and/or chest X-ray may be required depending on your intended length of stay in New Zealand. Check the Immigration New Zealand website for the current requirements based on your country of origin.
  • No previous STGWV or PSWV: You must not have previously been granted a Short-Term Graduate Work Visa or a Post Study Work Visa. Both visas are granted only once in a lifetime.
  • New Zealand Scholarship holders: If your study was supported under the New Zealand Scholarship Program, you must obtain written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand before applying.
  • Application timing: Your application must be submitted within 3 months of your New Zealand student visa expiring. Do not wait — late applications will not be accepted.

Key Conditions — What You Can and Cannot Do

The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa comes with specific conditions that all holders must understand before applying:

✅ Allowed
Open Work Rights
Work for any employer in any role under an employment agreement or contract for services. Full-time, part-time, or casual work is permitted.
✅ Allowed
Transition to AEWV
Use the 6 months to secure an employer willing to sponsor you for an Accredited Employer Work Visa — the main pathway to longer-term work in New Zealand.
❌ Not Allowed
Business Ownership
You cannot run your own business on this visa. All work must be carried out under an employment agreement or contract for services with an existing employer.
❌ Not Allowed
Partner / Child Work Visa Support
Short-Term Graduate Work Visa holders cannot sponsor a partner for a work visa or children for a Dependent Child Student Visa. Visitor visa applications may be possible separately.
💡
What counts as a re-entry student visa after holding this visa? If you hold, or have held, a Short-Term Graduate Work Visa, you can apply for a new student visa only if your proposed study is a bachelor's degree or a program at a higher NZQCF level than the qualification your STGWV was based on — and only if that new qualification makes you eligible for a Post Study Work Visa. This is an important restriction to plan around if further study in New Zealand is part of your long-term plan.

Post Study Work Visa — Eligibility Is Also Expanding from November 16, 2026

Alongside the new Short-Term Graduate Work Visa, Immigration New Zealand is simultaneously extending eligibility for the existing Post Study Work Visa to a new group of graduates. From November 16, 2026, graduates who completed a Graduate Diploma at NZQCF Level 7 will be eligible to apply for the Post Study Work Visa — provided they meet all of the following conditions:

  • Completed a Graduate Diploma at NZQCF Level 7 studied full-time in New Zealand for the full duration of the qualification.
  • Enrolled for the full duration — cross-crediting or recognition of prior learning (RPL) is not eligible. You must have completed the program in its entirety.
  • Hold a bachelor's degree — completed in New Zealand or overseas, with no time limit on when it was awarded. An International Qualification Assessment is not required for overseas bachelor's degrees, though Immigration New Zealand may check qualification authenticity.

The Post Study Work Visa for Graduate Diploma holders will be issued for the duration of time the student spent studying the Graduate Diploma in New Zealand — up to a maximum of one year. PSWV holders can support partners and dependent children for visitor, work, or dependent child student visas, making this a meaningfully more flexible visa than the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa.

📋
You can only ever hold one Post Study Work Visa Anyone who has already held a Post Study Work Visa in the past — even years ago — is not eligible for another, regardless of whether their new study is at the same or higher level. This applies equally to the new Graduate Diploma pathway.

Key Dates — What Happens and When

March 12, 2026
Immigration New Zealand First Announced the Changes
The initial announcement of the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa and expanded Post Study Work Visa eligibility was made. The November 16, 2026 launch date was confirmed on May 29, 2026 via the official Immigration New Zealand news center.
Now — October 2026
Plan Your Qualification and Post-Study Strategy
If you are currently studying in New Zealand or planning to start, review your qualification level against the NZQCF framework now. Determine whether you will qualify for the Post Study Work Visa or the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa — this changes your post-graduation planning significantly.
November 16, 2026
Both Visas Open for Applications
The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa begins accepting applications. The expanded Post Study Work Visa eligibility for Graduate Diploma holders also comes into effect on the same date. Apply as close to this date as possible if you are already eligible — do not wait until the end of your 3-month window.
Within 3 Months of Student Visa Expiry
Your Application Deadline
You must submit your Short-Term Graduate Work Visa application within three months of your New Zealand student visa expiring. Missing this window means you lose your eligibility entirely. Set a calendar reminder the day your student visa expires.
During Your 6-Month Visa
Secure an Accredited Employer Work Visa
Your primary goal during the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa period is to find an employer willing and able to sponsor you for an Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV). Start your job search before the visa is granted — not after it begins.

How to Use This Visa Strategically

Six months sounds short — but if you plan ahead, it is enough time to secure employer sponsorship and transition to a longer-term visa. Here is how to make the most of it:

  • Start your job search before you graduate: The most common mistake graduates make is waiting until their visa is approved to begin looking for work. Begin applying for roles in your final semester. By the time your Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is granted, you want to already have interviews underway or offers in progress.
  • Target employers who are AEWV accredited: Not all New Zealand employers hold Accredited Employer status with Immigration New Zealand. When applying for roles, check whether the employer is on the accredited employer register — only accredited employers can sponsor you for the AEWV that extends your stay beyond six months.
  • Understand the Green List: Certain occupations on New Zealand's Green List Tier 1 allow direct application for permanent residency via the Residence from Work pathway without a points test. If your qualification and intended role qualify, your post-graduation strategy should be shaped around this pathway from the start.
  • Have NZD $5,000 ready before you apply: The minimum fund requirement must be demonstrably available at the time of your application. Do not leave financial preparation to the last few weeks before your student visa expires.
  • Apply within the 3-month window — don't leave it late: The application must be submitted within 3 months of your student visa expiry. Processing takes time. Apply at the earliest opportunity after November 16, 2026 — not close to the deadline.

Frequently Asked Questions

When can I apply for the New Zealand Short-Term Graduate Work Visa?
Applications open on November 16, 2026, as confirmed by Immigration New Zealand on May 29, 2026. You must apply within 3 months of your New Zealand student visa expiring. If your student visa has already expired before November 16, 2026, you will not be able to apply retroactively — the visa is available only to graduates whose student visas are still valid or who are within the 3-month window after expiry on or after the launch date.
What is the difference between the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa and the Post Study Work Visa?
The Post Study Work Visa (PSWV) provides 1–3 years of open work rights and is available to graduates of NZQCF Level 7 bachelor's degrees and above. It also allows holders to support partners and dependent children. The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is a new, shorter visa — 6 months only, non-extendable — for graduates of NZQCF Level 5–7 qualifications that do not qualify for the PSWV. It cannot support partner or dependent child visas. Both are granted once only in a lifetime.
Can I apply for a second Short-Term Graduate Work Visa if I study again?
No — the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is a once-in-a-lifetime visa. You cannot apply for a second one under any circumstances. If you wish to study again in New Zealand after holding this visa, your new qualification must be a bachelor's degree or higher-level program that makes you eligible for a Post Study Work Visa — and you must not have previously held a Post Study Work Visa either.
Does the Short-Term Graduate Work Visa lead to permanent residency in New Zealand?
Not directly — but it can be the first step. During your 6-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa, your goal should be to secure employment with an accredited employer who can sponsor your Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV). Once on the AEWV, if your role is listed on New Zealand's Green List Tier 1, you may be able to apply for permanent residency through the Residence from Work pathway. The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa is a bridge to longer-term work rights — not a direct PR pathway itself.
